issues.reason: Comparatives & degree states a comparative 'does not entail the positive' (taller-than-Y doesn't make X tall), so the flat (Member standard_and_poors_500_index broad) asserts what the sentence does not say.

The Measures scale rule itself supplies a dimension noun whenever no adjective is stated ('weighs 5 kg' -> weight, 'costs $20' -> price — neither noun is in the text), so `increase` for 'was up' is the same licensed derivation, and the atom is true of the sentence's content in the delta gap the reviewer registers.

Same licence: `level` is the supplied dimension noun for a bare index value and `point` is the unit the clause's own '9.05 points' states, so both atoms are true and well-typed improvisation rather than defects.

Exactly one Name atom is licensed per proper noun and there is no alias/identifier head, so omitting <.SPX> is precisely what 'never invent a relation head or an unlicensed encoding to fill a coverage gap' requires.

gaps_confirmed: attributive comparative with an elided standard ('the broader Index') — only predicative 'X is ADJ-er than Y' with an explicit Y is covered
delta / change-of-value measures ('was up 9.05 points') — Measure has no change form and no licensed scale word for up/down
'or' as an appositive restatement of one value in another unit ('9.05 points, or 0.94 percent') — the Disjunction section would wrongly make this an opaque (Or …)
a parenthetical ticker / alias beside a proper name (<.SPX>) — exactly one Name atom is licensed and there is no alias relation
new_gaps: a bare numeric level with no stated dimension noun and no stated unit ('at 972.64') — both the Measure scale and the unit must be supplied, which the surface-dimension rule does not license
building a name symbol from a name containing an ampersand, an apostrophe and digits ('Standard & Poor's 500 Index' -> standard_and_poors_500_index) is unspecified
repair_summary: Removed (Member standard_and_poors_500_index broad) — with the comparative's standard elided there is no licensed More encoding, so the offending positive atom is deleted rather than replaced.
notes: Treating the appositive 'or' as two coexisting measures rather than an (Or …) is the right call, and the Kestrel-River name/kind split is applied correctly.
